name: L1e-A Powered Cycle, up to 1 kW and 25 km/h
description: The powered cycle of Regulation (EU) No 168/2013 the classifications naming this group share: a cycle designed to pedal whose auxiliary propulsion of no more than 1,000 W mainly aids pedalling and cuts off by 25 km/h. A vehicle carries this group's id in place of each classification in it, and each of those holds its own jurisdiction's licence, registration, insurance, helmet and riding rules.

restrictions.rule: A cycle designed to pedal, with an auxiliary propulsion whose primary aim is to aid pedalling
The auxiliary propulsion's output cuts off at a vehicle speed of 25 km/h or less
Maximum continuous rated or net power of 1,000 W or less
Two wheels, or three or four as a powered cycle technically equivalent to a two-wheeler, and no more than 4,000 mm long, 1,000 mm wide and 2,500 mm tall
Its propulsion needn't cut out when the rider stops pedalling, so it may have a throttle, and needn't be electric
Past the EPAC's limits: a pedal cycle with no more than 250 W whose motor assists only while pedalled and cuts off before 25 km/h is outside the Regulation instead
One past any of these criteria falls to the next L1e category it meets, the L1e-B two-wheel moped
